terms.meaning: the stage of an application, such as sourced or applied

used_by: Likely the root route of the app, since the ingest page returns here after saving.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the home page
sections.what: Brings in the status list, score bar, status pill, shared header and footer, the application functions and the profile check.
sections.why: The home page reads, shows and deletes applications and checks whether a profile exists.
sections.watch_out: The profile check may decide what new users see, and that logic is not visible here.

sections.name: AppCard
sections.title: Single application card
sections.what: Shows one job application as a card with the company, role, location, remote tag, status, score bar, bucket, and capture date. Clicking the card opens that application, and a small x button deletes it.
sections.why: Lets the user see the key facts of each application at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The delete button only appears to work when the application has an id, so entries without an id cannot be removed from here.

sections.name: Dashboard (part 1)
sections.title: Dashboard data and summary numbers
sections.what: Loads saved applications when the page opens and sends users without a profile to the onboarding page. Calculates the active count, average score, interview rate, and count per status, and refreshes when data changes.
sections.why: Keeps the numbers and cards up to date when applications change elsewhere.
sections.watch_out: The interview rate counts interview and offer results out of all applications, including rejected ones, so it is not a rate among active applications.

sections.name: Dashboard (part 2)
sections.title: Pipeline columns and action buttons
sections.what: Shows the SCAN PORTALS and INGEST JD buttons, then one column per status holding the matching cards. A column with no cards shows a NO APPLICATIONS note.
sections.why: Groups applications by stage so the user sees where each one stands.
sections.watch_out: Cards are keyed by their list position instead of their id, so the list order must stay stable to avoid display mix-ups.

summary: Likely the home page of the app, which lists saved job applications with their status and scores and can delete them. Only the imports were visible.
purpose: Likely the main pipeline view, the page the app returns to after saving a job.
why: Likely reason: the ingest page sends the user back here after saving, so this is probably the main list.
how: Only the imports are visible. They bring in the status list, score bar, status pill, shared header and footer, application load and delete functions, and a profile check. The rest is not visible.
inputs: Saved applications, and the profile check (inferred from imports).
risks: Deletion is wired in, and this file does not show whether it asks for confirmation.
debug: If the list is empty, check the saved application data. If deletion fails, check the store functions it calls.
